teaser.text: Canadian Natural Resources Ltd. is an energy producer that sells oil and natural gas to industrial buyers. Its money comes in when those products are delivered, and goes out through production, transportation, royalties, investment, financing, taxes and eventual cleanup.

stock.title: Canadian Natural Resources stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Canadian Natural Resources stock forecast: weighted price C$90.70 in October 2027, plus bear, base and bull cases and cash-flow context.
stock.opening: The weighted Canadian Natural Resources scenario is C$90.70 in October 2027, with C$87.66 in October 2029. It hinges on normalized prices, modest growth and cash generation sufficient to reduce debt.
stock.closing: The full Canadian Natural Resources memo also explains its business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Canadian Natural Resources' shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast's central case is a positive return, but not a narrow one. The probability-weighted price is C$90.70 in October 2027 and C$88.44 in October 2028. It is C$87.66 in October 2029.

The bear case carries a 25% probability and the base case 55%. The bull case carries 20%. The November 5, 2026 results release tests the Horizon turnaround. Definitive policy agreements are targeted for November 15, 2026. A C$5,637 million debt maturity in year two tests refinancing and cash flexibility. T-Block cessation in Q1 2027 and NRUTT’s targeted Q3 2027 completion test project delivery. Sustained SCO premiums would support the growth case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Canadian Natural Resources, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The base path assumes 3% volume growth initially, then 2% annually, consistent with management's 2026 production target. It also assumes oil prices below the Q2 average but above the 2025 realized level. The bear case combines weaker prices, higher costs and declining volumes. The bull case assumes stronger realizations and faster growth, despite gradual price normalization.

blocks.heading: How much does Canadian Natural Resources pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The current annualized dividend is C$2.50. The base case raises it to C$2.60 in the first window, then C$2.85 and C$3.10. The bear case freezes it at C$2.50 because debt and closure spending absorb cash. The bull case reaches C$3.75 by 2029, requiring stronger cash generation and potentially slower buybacks.

blocks.heading: Does Canadian Natural Resources cover its dividend with cash?

paragraphs.text: The pattern is clear: CNQ distributed much of its surplus while its balance sheet was improving, then used debt to help fund the 2024 acquisition. In 2025, free cash flow again covered dividends and buybacks while net debt fell. CNQ repurchased approximately 33.5 million shares in 2025. The weighted average price was C$43.28, which shows what it paid but not whether the repurchases were good investments.

Cash generation is strong, but free cash flow depends on what the analyst subtracts. Operating cash flow was C$15,106 million in 2025. After capital spending and lease payments, an analytical free-cash-flow figure was C$9,038 million.

blocks.heading: What could change the Canadian Natural Resources dividend?

paragraphs.text: The March 2026 policy makes the choice between debt reduction and buybacks explicit. The regular dividend rose to C$0.625 per quarter. CNQ directs 60% of its policy measure to buybacks when net debt is at least C$16 billion, 75% between C$13 billion and C$16 billion, and 100% at or below C$13 billion. Management discussed reaching the lower threshold in early 2027 at then-current prices. The real test is whether payouts leave enough flexibility when oil prices weaken.

blocks.heading: What is Canadian Natural Resources' dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: Including dividends, those outcomes represent gains of 22% and 23% in the first two years. The three-year gain is 26%. The 2029 bear-to-bull range runs from C$41.77 to C$142.29. Today's price is C$76.46.

blocks.heading: Has Canadian Natural Resources kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Canadian Natural has delivered production, debt reduction and fewer shares outstanding. Whether it is truly on shareholders’ side will depend on whether future rewards reflect safety, balance-sheet resilience and the results of the acquisitions that earned them.

blocks.heading: What has Canadian Natural Resources reported in its last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: The surrounding quarters were less clean. December 2025 included the AOSP gain, while September 2025 included the major North Sea charge. March 2026 showed steadier company-adjusted earnings. The June result therefore demonstrates strong capacity, but not a normal profit rate.

blocks.heading: What should Canadian Natural Resources watch in its next results?

paragraphs.text: November brings two tests: whether operations delivered and whether governments made larger expansion investable. The November 5 results release should show the initial effect of Horizon’s turnaround, but because the shutdown extended into October, the quarter alone cannot establish the full result.

stock.opening: Le scénario pondéré de Canadian Natural Resources donne 90,70 $ CA en octobre 2027, puis 87,66 $ CA en octobre 2029. Il repose sur des prix normalisés, une croissance modeste et une génération de trésorerie suffisante pour réduire la dette.
stock.closing: Le dossier complet sur Canadian Natural Resources explique aussi ses activités, ses rivales, sa direction et ses risques.

blocks.heading: Où l’action de Canadian Natural Resources pourrait-elle se trouver en 2029?

paragraphs.text: Le scénario baissier se voit attribuer une probabilité de 25 % et le scénario de base, de 55 %. Le scénario haussier se voit attribuer 20 %. La publication des résultats du 5 novembre 2026 mettra à l’épreuve le redressement de Horizon. La conclusion d’ententes définitives sur les politiques est ciblée pour le 15 novembre 2026. Une échéance de dette de 5 637 millions $ CA en deuxième année met à l’épreuve le refinancement et la souplesse de la trésorerie. La cessation de T-Block au T1 2027 et l’achèvement ciblé de NRUTT au T3 2027 mettront à l’épreuve l’exécution des projets. Le maintien de primes sur le SCO appuierait le scénario de croissance.

blocks.heading: Que doit-il arriver pour que Canadian Natural Resources réussisse, et qu’est-ce qui pourrait mal tourner?

paragraphs.text: La trajectoire de base suppose une croissance initiale des volumes de 3 %, puis de 2 % par année, ce qui concorde avec la cible de production de la direction pour 2026. Elle suppose aussi des prix du pétrole inférieurs à la moyenne du T2, mais supérieurs au niveau réalisé en 2025. Le scénario baissier combine des prix plus faibles, des coûts plus élevés et des volumes en baisse. Le scénario haussier suppose de meilleures réalisations et une croissance plus rapide, malgré une normalisation graduelle des prix.

blocks.heading: Canadian Natural Resources couvre-t-elle son dividende avec ses liquidités?

paragraphs.text: Le schéma est clair : CNQ a distribué une grande partie de son surplus alors que son bilan s’améliorait, puis a eu recours à la dette pour contribuer au financement de l’acquisition de 2024. En 2025, le flux de trésorerie disponible a de nouveau couvert les dividendes et les rachats d’actions, tandis que la dette nette diminuait. CNQ a racheté environ 33,5 millions d’actions en 2025. Le prix moyen pondéré était de 43,28 $ CA, ce qui montre combien elle a payé, mais pas si les rachats constituaient de bons investissements.

La génération de liquidités est solide, mais le flux de trésorerie disponible dépend de ce que l’analyste soustrait. Les flux de trésorerie liés aux activités d’exploitation se sont établis à 15 106 millions $ CA en 2025. Après les dépenses en immobilisations et les paiements de loyers, le flux de trésorerie disponible calculé par l’analyste s’élevait à 9 038 millions $ CA.

blocks.heading: Qu’est-ce qui pourrait changer le dividende de Canadian Natural Resources?

paragraphs.text: La politique de mars 2026 rend explicite le choix entre la réduction de la dette et les rachats d’actions. Le dividende régulier est passé à 0,625 $ CA par trimestre. CNQ affecte 60 % de sa mesure de référence aux rachats d’actions lorsque la dette nette atteint au moins 16 milliards $ CA, 75 % lorsqu’elle se situe entre 13 milliards $ CA et 16 milliards $ CA, et 100 % lorsqu’elle est de 13 milliards $ CA ou moins. La direction a évoqué l’atteinte du seuil inférieur au début de 2027, aux cours alors en vigueur. Le véritable test consiste à déterminer si les distributions laissent suffisamment de marge de manœuvre lorsque les prix du pétrole fléchissent.
